headline: Within 10–20 years, almost everything except land approaches near-zero cost. Six independent voices say this. One sceptic dissents.

quotes.author: Elon Musk
quotes.quote: In 10 to 20 years, work will be optional and money will be irrelevant. Universal high income — you can have whatever you want.

quotes.author: Sam Altman
quotes.quote: The costs of intelligence and energy are going to be on a path towards near-zero. By 2030, it will become clear that the AI revolution and renewable+nuclear energy are going to get us there.

quotes.author: Michael Saylor
quotes.quote: Automation and AI will drive a 100-fold rise in productivity. Investors have roughly 10 years to stake their claim in the new economy.

categories.name: Intelligence / digital
categories.mechanism: Compute on Wright's Law (20-30%/doubling). LLM inference cost already falling 10x/yr. Approaches utility pricing.

categories.name: Energy

checkpoints.anchor: Seba: solar+wind+battery cheaper than fossil everywhere

categories.mechanism: Solar PV 20%/doubling Wright curve, batteries 18-35%/doubling. Storage solves intermittency. Energy as utility flat-fee.

categories.name: Transport

categories.mechanism: EV cost decline + autonomous removes driver wages + fleet utilisation 10x. RethinkX: $1T/yr returned to US consumers by 2030.

categories.name: Manufactured goods
categories.mechanism: Tesla Optimus pays back vs human labour in <1 year. Robotic assembly + AI design + 3D printing. Bounded by raw materials.

categories.name: Food (proteins)
categories.mechanism: Lab-grown meat at $17/lb today, parity with conventional ($5/lb) by 2030. Vertical farms 80% less land, 90% less water.

categories.name: Education

checkpoints.anchor: Content delivery free; networking premium remains

categories.mechanism: AI tutors deflate content delivery to ~zero. Networking and credentialing value sticky. Bottom-tier schools first to collapse.

categories.name: Apparel
categories.mechanism: BLS: apparel CPI -0.5%/yr in early 2026. Robotic textile + on-demand printing eliminates labour and inventory cost.

categories.name: Food (general groceries)
categories.mechanism: Vertical farming 80% less land, 90% less water. Slower than proteins because more land-bound for grains/produce.

categories.name: Healthcare
categories.mechanism: AI diagnostics + drug discovery + robotic surgery offset historical +4.5%/yr inflation. Aging demographics counter. Slowest of the deflators.

categories.name: Services (hospitality, care)

checkpoints.anchor: First-wave service robots in fast food, hotels, basic care
Optimus-class robots in housekeeping, food prep, eldercare
Most service work robotic; humans for premium / specialty only
Service largely free at the floor; human-touch is luxury

categories.mechanism: Reversed — Steve's view that services go mostly robotic. Optimus + dedicated kitchen/cleaning bots replace most service labour. Premium human-touch persists as luxury but the floor approaches free.

categories.name: LAND

checkpoints.anchor: Major scarce resource of the abundance era

categories.mechanism: Fixed supply. As everything else falls toward zero, abundance wealth bids up the only thing that can't be made more of. Knoll-Schularick: 80% of post-WWII house boom is LAND, not structures.

skeptic.author: Daron Acemoglu
skeptic.estimate: Only 0.53–0.66% total TFP gain over 10 years from AI
skeptic.argument: Only 20% of US labour tasks exposed; even fewer profitably automatable. Hulten's theorem applied to actual task-level cost savings. Bulls overestimate because early evidence is from easy-to-learn tasks; harder tasks deliver less.

scenarios.name: AXION projection (planning assumption)

Services + manual waves: humanoid robots at scale; 85% of today's jobs gone

workforce_composition.title: Today's jobs displaced by 2035
workforce_composition.intro: Past automation waves (steam, electricity, computing) hit physical labour first while knowledge work expanded. AI inverts the order: knowledge work is being displaced FIRST, services and manual labour follow together when humanoid robotics scale (Optimus-class, ~2030). Each category loses ~85% of its workers under this trajectory — could be 75% or 90%, outcome is basically the same.

workforce_composition.transition_gap: 85% displacement does NOT mean 85% permanent unemployment. Many displaced workers will find new work in emergent categories that don't yet exist — AI supervision, premium human-touch service, novel craft, community and relational roles, AI-curated experience design. (60% of 2025 jobs didn't exist in 1940.) AXION's role is to handle the TRANSITION GAP — supporting people during the period between losing their old role and finding the new one — and provide UBI as a permanent floor for those for whom no replacement role emerges.

displacement_evidence.intro: Cost ratios for AI tools versus human labour, in 2026. Sources cited where available; ranges given to reflect uncertainty between peak-scenario (knowledgeable user, well-defined task) and typical-team use. Caveat below explains why most figures are conservative.
displacement_evidence.caveat: These are productivity ratios with cited sources, not full-replacement ratios. The bull intuition that 'one architect with Claude Code replaces a 13-person business-software team' may well be true at the OUTPUT level — the AI is capable — but the rate-limits and context window of a $90 Pro subscription likely cannot sustain that workload; heavy use needs Max 20× ($200/mo) or API access at higher cost. So the ratios below reflect **what existing studies and case data actually demonstrate**, not extrapolations. Five other roles (content, illustration, translation, legal review, data entry) were dropped from this table because no rigorous evidence was available — the displacement is happening but the magnitude isn't measured.

examples.human_baseline: Productivity uplift on 1 senior engineer (~$108K/yr); $90 enables ~1.5-1.8× output, replaces ~half a dev's cost
examples.evidence: Anthropic's own engineers (Aug 2025 internal study, 132 engineers + 53 interviews + 200K transcripts): 50% average productivity gain; 67% increase in merged PRs per engineer per day after Claude Code rollout. GitHub Copilot peer-reviewed (Microsoft Research / arXiv 2023): 55.8% faster on controlled coding task, 95% CI [21%, 89%].
examples.note: Anthropic's data measures their OWN frontier-research engineering — the hardest case for AI. For typical enterprise CRUD the productivity gain is likely much higher (the patterns are well-trodden) but I have no rigorous study to cite, so this row stays at the conservative measured number. The bull case for software is real; this row is its FLOOR.

examples.human_baseline: Hybrid model: AI handles 60-70%, humans handle complex 30-40%
examples.evidence: Klarna 2024: AI handled 2.3M conversations in first month, equivalent to 700 full-time agents. $40M annual savings projected at announcement. PARTIALLY REVERSED 2025 — customer satisfaction dropped on complex cases; humans rehired for edge cases. Stable hybrid (~67% AI / 33% human) is the actual deployment a year later.
examples.note: Initial pure-replacement attempt failed on quality. The hybrid is what worked. Real headcount savings ~50%, not 100%. Cautionary tale: AI can match volume but not always quality on complex/emotional cases.

examples.evidence: ChatGPT consumer adoption: 300M+ weekly active users by late 2025 — many querying it on personal finance instead of booking IFA appointments. Robo-advisers (Wealthfront, Betterment): AUM grew 5× since 2022 to ~$80B+. Vanguard Personal Advisor and similar AI-augmented services serve millions. UK FCA 2025 statements noted material decline in High-Street IFA usage among under-50s.
examples.note: Observed market behaviour, not a peer-reviewed productivity study. The displacement is real and large — peer review lags by years. Human advisers are retreating to high-net-worth and emotional/behavioural counselling.

displacement_evidence.macro_summary: Anthropic Claude Code revenue: $1B annualised (Nov 2025), ~$2B (Jan 2026). Anthropic Economic Index (March 2026): 4% of jobs use AI for 75%+ of tasks; augmentation 52% > automation 45%. The three rows above are what is actually MEASURED in 2026. The bull intuition — that displacement is much larger and broader than these rigorous numbers suggest — may well be right, but the table doesn't claim numbers it can't back.
displacement_evidence.axion_implication: Even at the conservative measured ratios shown above, capital-share-of-AI-gains is heavily skewed: Anthropic captures ~$90/user/month, customers capture ~50× that in displaced wage cost. Multiplied across millions of users, the founder-class capture is real and growing. It is the levy base that the AXION synthesis depends on.

profitability.framework: Acemoglu-Restrepo task-based model: AI productivity gains are distributed across three claimants — capital (margins expand), consumer (prices fall), or labour (new tasks emerge at higher wages). The three scenarios below describe how the EXTERNAL economy may evolve. See the AXION insulation panel below — internally, the colony's pegged basket means citizens experience price stability regardless of which scenario plays out.

scenarios.name: AXION projection (capital-extreme, planning case)
scenarios.anchor: Most aggressive capital capture. Automation winners take outsize share; labour share collapses near-zero; consumers benefit through cheaper goods but slowly. This is what AXION colonies plan for.
scenarios.axion_implication: Largest levy pool. Margins expand toward 50%+. Founder-class capture concentrated. AXION math closes earliest under this scenario — MS1 around 2032, MS2 by 2038.

scenarios.name: Capital-heavy capture (current US trajectory)
scenarios.anchor: Restrepo (Yale): half of labor share decline since 1980s from automation. McKinsey: $2.6-4.4T/yr to corporate profits.
scenarios.axion_implication: Profit pool grows substantially. Levy capacity high. UBI obligation stays high (prices fall slowly). Both scale up together.

scenarios.name: Consumer-heavy capture (competitive markets)
scenarios.anchor: Bull thesis: prices crash 85% by 2045 means consumer captures most gains. Profit pool grows modestly in $. Margins flat-to-slightly-up.
scenarios.axion_implication: Levy pool small in $. But UBI obligation also collapses (basket falls 85%). Both small together. Math closes IF trajectories align.

scenarios.name: Labor-rebalanced (new tasks emerge fast)
scenarios.anchor: Acemoglu's 'new task creation' channel; historical pattern (60% of 2025 jobs didn't exist in 1940).
scenarios.axion_implication: Wages grow with AI. UBI less urgent — most citizens still employed at higher real wages. Levy from corporate profit modest but adequate for residual welfare.

axion_insulation.title: Why this debate is insulated from AXION — the basket peg
axion_insulation.summary: The capital-vs-consumer-vs-labour debate is about who captures AI productivity gains in the EXTERNAL fiat economy. AXION is a parallel economy whose internal currency (MOND) is pegged to the basket. Citizens pay the same number of MOND for the same goods, year after year, regardless of external profit-share dynamics.
mechanism: A fixed composition of essential goods and services (food, energy, transport, structure-rent, etc.). Composition is set; quantities are pegged.
1 basket-unit = 1 MOND. The peg is maintained by Fisc reserves, not market arbitrage. Citizens experience stable prices in S regardless of USD volatility.

When external prices fall (consumer-capture scenario), the USD value of an MOND rises. When external prices rise (capital-capture), MOND's USD value falls. The colony absorbs the FX volatility; the citizen does not.
Levy is collected on internal S-denominated transactions. Levy revenue in S is a function of internal commerce, not external macro split.
UBI obligation in S is fixed by basket × multiplier × citizens. Stable internally regardless of which external scenario plays out.
axion_insulation.implication: The three scenarios above tell us what to expect in the OUTSIDE world and inform inter-colony trade pricing. Inside the colony, daily life is shielded by design. This is the central reason a parallel economy exists at all — to provide stability that the external fiat system, amid AI-driven price disruption, cannot guarantee.

political_economy.title: Why capital pays the levy — the Henry Ford insight
political_economy.tension: Capital owners will fight to retain margins. They'll lobby against tax, relocate operations, optimise for evasion. The naïve view of the AXION levy treats it as adversarial — capital vs colony, zero-sum.
political_economy.alignment: The deeper truth: capital cannot realise its margins without consumers. Automation eliminates the wage channel that historically funded consumer demand. Without an alternative, capital faces a customer-base extinction event — high margins on zero sales is zero profit. The levy is what keeps the consumer base solvent.
political_economy.precedent: Henry Ford, 1914: paid $5/day (double prevailing wage) so his own workers could afford the cars he was producing. Not philanthropy — pure capital preservation. The AXION levy is the same idea at societal scale: capital funds the income that funds its own revenues.
political_economy.design_implication: AXION's cost-neutral MS1 design lowers the political cost of switch-on — the State loses nothing because AXION just takes over existing welfare obligations. Once that channel is open, scaling toward MS2 becomes a growth conversation, not a tax conversation. Capital prefers a managed levy over: civil unrest, mass policy intervention, or revolution.

key_quote.text: It is not the employer who pays the wages. Employers only handle the money. It is the customer who pays the wages.
key_quote.author: Henry Ford, 1922

political_economy.axion_principle: The AXION levy is not a tax ON capital — it is a service fee FOR ACCESS to consumers whose income capital itself ultimately funds. Reframed this way, capital's rational stance is to support the levy, not resist it.
